title: Unbounded Channel Allocation (Unbounded Queue)
pattern: Invoking `tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel` or similar unbounded channel creation constructors without bounding maximum capacity.
why_bad: Unbounded channels allow producers to queue an infinite number of messages, causing memory consumption to grow linearly with queue size [46]. If consumers are slower than producers or block temporarily, the system will eventually crash with an Out of Memory (OOM) error [46, 583]. A bounded queue or channel provides backpressure, forcing the producer to slow down or fail fast [46, 583].
detection: Identify calls to channel constructors that create unbounded channels (e.g., `mpsc::unbounded_channel()`, `crossbeam::channel::unbounded()`) without any associated limit or configuration.
fix: Use a bounded channel with an explicit capacity, enabling backpressure or returning a `Full` error to producers [46].
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 8 (Backpressure) / passage [46]; Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 29 / passage [583].
